policies.policySummary: The Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007, provides a framework for the regulation, administration, and incentivization of mining activities in Nigeria. The act governs the exploration, exploitation, and management of minerals in Nigeria. Ownership and control of minerals, water, and related resources are vested in the state. The exploration or exploitation of minerals requires proper authority. Certain lands are excluded from mineral exploration and exploitation. Priority and competitive bidding processes for mineral rights.
policies.institutionalResponsibility:
The Minister of Mines and Steel Development oversees the implementation of the Act.
Establishment of the Mining Cadastre Office and its zonal offices to manage mineral titles and maintain registers.
Creation of departments such as the Mines Inspectorate Department and Mines Environmental Compliance Department.
Establishment of State Mineral Resources and Environmental Management Committees.
Regulations and delegation of powers by the Minister

policies.policySummary: Federal Government of Nigeria, which holds ownership and control of all mineral resources in trust for the people under the Constitution (Section 44(3)) and the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007 (NMMA). The Minerals and Mining Regulations 2011 establish rules to regulate the acquisition, operation, and management of mineral titles in Nigeria. It outlines obligations for environmental protection, safety standards, environmental compliance, waste disposal, community compensation, and corporate social responsibility in mining operations. Establishment of the Solid Minerals Development Fund to drive investment and growth in the mining sector

policies.policyName: Roadmap for the Growth and Development of the Nigerian Mining Industry
policies.policySummary: Strategic plan to reposition mining as growth engine; identifies seven priority minerals, including lithium and niobium, and targets midstream processing and local value chains by 2025.
policies.esgElements: Limited; mostly focused on investment rather than ESG
policies.implementationChallenges: Funding, lack of coordination among MDAs

policies.policySummary: NGSA-led programme to generate modern geophysical and geochemical data for priority minerals, including gold, PGM, nickel, chromium, cobolt, rare earth minerals, lead zinc, silver, copper, barite and iron ore resources in Nigeria.
Environmental standards for mining operations covering waste, emissions, water, hazardous materials and rehabilitation.
policies.esgElements: Pollution control, water quality, tailings safety
policies.governanceIssues: Weak enforcement, agency overlap with MMSD

policies.policyName: Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) Formalisation Programme
policies.policySummary: Programme to support formalisation, training, environmental management and licensing of ASM cooperatives; aims to reduce illegal mining and improve traceability.
policies.governanceIssues: Weak incentives for formalisation, corruption barriers

policies.policySummary: Establishes NGSA’s mandate for geological mapping, exploration data generation, archival management and national geoscience database governance.
policies.governanceIssues: Legacy colonial data not digitised; poor data access

policies.policySummary: Nigeria’s domestic implementation of the EITI Standard, requiring revenue reporting, licence register transparency, beneficial ownership disclosure and audits.

policies.policyName: State Mining Policies & Mineral Development Companies
policies.policySummary: States have created mining development companies and local regulations to participate in joint ventures, regulate community agreements and support ASM cooperatives.
Mandatory agreements between mining companies and host communities outlining benefits, compensation, employment and social investment obligations.
policies.governanceIssues: Weak monitoring, elite capture within communities
